title: Pacific Fusion receives N.M. radioactive materials license
html:
The New Mexico Environment Department (NMED) has approved Pacific Fusion’s radioactive materials license, allowing it to fabricate and test deuterium-tritium fusion targets and conduct experiments at a facility that is under construction in Albuquerque, N.M., the company announced.

The license authorizes up to 15,000 curies (around 1.5 grams) of tritium, although the company said it “never intends to have an inventory that exceeds 10,000 curies.” The license also authorizes the use of materials needed to store tritium and support diagnostics and fusion operations.
